response.justification: The candidate is an experienced, versatile senior engineer (15+ years) with strong fundamentals, testing culture, and open-source contributions, but the profile does not match this role's mandatory requirements. C++ exposure is limited to roughly six months at National Instruments (2014–2015) and a university thesis project — far short of the required 5–10 years of hands-on C++ on Windows. The stack is overwhelmingly web/JavaScript/TypeScript/DLang, with no SQL Server or Oracle experience listed (only generic SQL/MySQL/MongoDB), no Windows platform focus, and no fixed income, derivatives, or capital-markets domain work. RIDE Capital offers tangential fintech exposure, but it was Node/GraphQL product work rather than investment-banking systems. The gap on the two hard requirements is too large to bridge in an interview.
strengths: Broad 15+ year engineering career with strong software craftsmanship, TDD, and CI/CD practice
Some low-level/performance experience (high-throughput services, async I/O, fibers) and C/C++ at National Instruments
Excellent communication evidenced by conference talks, workshops, and course authoring
concerns: C++ experience is roughly six months, a decade ago — nowhere near the required 5–10 years
No fixed income, derivatives, or investment-banking/capital-markets domain experience
No SQL Server/Oracle or Windows-platform development background; stack is web/TypeScript-centric

key_factors.factor: Windows platform and SQL Server/Oracle experience
